resolutions.fix: check_boilerplate_plumbing was rewritten from a question-asking check into an ALLOW-LIST, and came out shorter than what it replaced. WIRE_UI (6 expressions), WIRE_HANDLER (3, one per endpoint, matched inside that handler's own slice) and WIRE_API (1) pin every expression that carries the checkbox's value from the DOM to extract_items; each must appear exactly once. Matching is whitespace-insensitive (the same argument as anchor.py's core_of) but token-exact, so reformatting survives and a semantic edit does not. The reviewer's acceptance asked for 'no `not`/`!=`/constant between the read and the kwarg'; an allow-list was chosen over that block-list deliberately, because a block-list only ever bans the inversions somebody already thought of, and this is the third round in which the next unbanned one was found.
resolutions.covered_by: M1, M2, M3 and the unwired-fourth-mode shape in ui-boilerplate-wire-values (pair B, exact count 7); M4 in ui-boilerplate-exclusion-regression (pair A) shape 3; M5 in pair B via the shadowing shape. Each observed red individually against real-file copies before being claimed covered: M1 1, M2 1, M3 1, M4 1, M5 1, control 0. R2's original four shapes were re-run against the rewritten check and are still red (2, 1, 1, 1).
resolutions.two_pairs_because: The shapes conflict per slot — one handler cannot be both renamed and inverted, one file holds one excludeBp definition — so sixteen shapes do not fit in one pair without giving up the exact count that makes a regressed over-fire visible.

resolutions.note: The coordinator asked where the property had relocated after this repair, so four attacks were written against the ALLOW-LIST itself rather than against the hops it pins. Three passed it and were then closed: (A) a second `function excludeBp(){ return true; }` after the pinned one — the pin is satisfied and the shadow binds at runtime, closed by UNIQUE_UI requiring the definition sites themselves to be unique; (D) `<input type="checkbox" id="exclude-bp" disabled>` — every hop intact, capability unreachable, closed by a `disabled` check beside the existing `checked` one; (E) a call site commented out with its pinned expression left in the file as dead text, closed by matching against the file's LIVE text (whole-line `//`, HTML `<!-- -->`, and `#` for Python only — `#` is not stripped from the UI because the stylesheet is full of `#id{...}` selectors that start a line with it). The fourth, (F) a fourth `/api/extract/paste` mode that never wires the flag, was already caught by the route-set pin added in the same rewrite. All four are now committed shapes in pair A or pair B rather than notes. The level ABOVE this one — a pinned expression that is present, live, and never REACHED, e.g. its `$("#go-fx").onclick` binding deleted — is not closed, is named in the debt row, and is the honest ceiling of a textual check. A fifth hole was then closed on the same reasoning, unprompted: nothing pinned the header label, so the INVERSE of R5 — text stripped silently, with no 'boilerplate hidden' on screen — was as invisible as R5 itself. That expression is now pinned too (shape 9 of pair A), and deleting it from the real index.html goes red.
